subject: Re: Marketplace SKU + pricing guardrails — approvals needed (AWS/GCP refresh)
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Marketplace SKU + pricing guardrails — approvals needed (AWS/GCP refresh)

Hi Jordan,

We need CRO + Finance/RevRec + Legal sign-off on the SKU/pricing guardrails and discount policy for AWS/GCP marketplace before we finalize the public listing + private offer templates.

Summary of what we’re proposing (v2):

1) Public listing (self-serve):
- Hosted API (usage-based): billed by tokens/embedding units via marketplace metering.
- “Starter” positioning only; no custom commit in the public listing.

2) Private offers (sales-assisted):
- Hosted API Commit (annual): customer commits to $/year spend via marketplace; usage draws down.
- Dedicated Capacity (reserved): priced per GPU-hour equivalent / capacity unit; includes SLA tier.
- Private Deployment (license + support): platform fee + support tier (metered as contract dimension where allowed).

Guardrails we need confirmed:
- Minimums: Hosted commit minimum $120k/yr; Dedicated minimum $250k/yr; Private minimum $400k/yr (plus SOW).
- Discounting: standard discount bands by term length + volume; max discount cap; approval workflow.
- Credits/trials: whether we allow any “free credits” through marketplace (my recommendation: no; keep credits off-marketplace and handled as Redwood promotional credits in-product).

Open questions from GTM:
- Do we allow 2-year/3-year commits through marketplace? If yes, do we require annual invoicing vs upfront?
- Are we comfortable with “commit drawdown” language from a revrec perspective (esp. on AWS)?
- Refund/credit handling if a customer cancels marketplace subscription mid-term (what can we say in templates)?

Attachments:
- sku-mapping-and-pricing-working-sheet.xlsx
- marketplace-sku-catalog-v2.pdf
- aws-private-offer-template-notes.docx

If we can align today, Partnerships can lock the offer structure and we can keep the submission timeline.

Thanks,
Soojin
Director, Product Marketing
Redwood Inference


---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU + pricing guardrails — approvals needed (AWS/GCP refresh)

Thanks. We should keep this simple + enforceable for AEs.

My asks for Finance/RevRec/Legal:
1) Confirm minimums (or propose alternate) and whether they apply per cloud marketplace or global.
2) Confirm discount cap for marketplace private offers (I’m leaning: 0–15% standard; 15–25% w/ CRO+Finance; >25% requires CEO/Finance exception).
3) Confirm policy on promo credits: I agree w/ “no marketplace credits.” If we must do something, we do it as a Redwood-side credit with explicit limits.

Soojin — can you also add language in the doc on:
- No “price match” promises in offer templates.
- Dedicated includes *reserved* capacity not “unlimited.”

Laura/Emily/Sofia — please reply with sign-off or required changes by EOD. We need to push templates to Partnerships tomorrow.

Jordan
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference


---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 12:26 PM
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU + pricing guardrails — approvals needed (AWS/GCP refresh)

Agree with direction. A few finance guardrails we need to bake in:

Minimums
- Hosted commit: $120k/yr minimum is fine.
- Dedicated: $250k/yr minimum is fine but add an explicit floor on effective $/GPU-hr equivalent (we’ve seen marketplace deals come in with aggressive “headline discounts” that blow margin).
- Private: $400k/yr minimum is fine; I’d prefer “starting at $400k/yr” language (since support + services vary).

Discounting / approvals
- I’m OK with your proposed bands, with one tweak:
  - 0–15%: AE + Sales Director approval (documented in HubSpot)
  - 15–25%: CRO + Finance
  - >25%: CRO + Finance + CEO (exception)
- Also: any “non-standard payment terms” (net > 30) should require Finance approval even if discount <15%.

Credits
- Strong preference: no credits through marketplace.
- If GTM needs a lever: Redwood-issued promotional credits only, time-bound (30–60 days), with explicit cap and approval from CRO.

Also flagging that marketplace fees differ by channel; keep pricing sheets aligned to a margin floor and don’t let reps apply both a rate card discount + a separate “marketplace concession.”

Laura Bennett
Finance (Pricing)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 1:41 PM
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU + pricing guardrails — approvals needed (AWS/GCP refresh)

RevRec POV (high level; details are in the marketplace revrec notes page):

1) “Commit drawdown” language
- OK to describe operationally (customer commits; usage draws down) BUT avoid implying the customer is purchasing “prepaid tokens” that are refundable.
- We should use consistent terms: “committed spend” / “committed usage amount” and reference marketplace contract terms for cancellation/refunds.

2) Multi-year marketplace commits
- We can support 2-year/3-year private offers.
- Preference is annual invoicing (or annual contract dimensions) rather than full upfront unless the marketplace channel forces it.
- If any offer includes an upfront component, ensure the template includes a clear delivery/performance obligation description.

3) Cancellation / refunds
- We should not promise refunds; defer to AWS/GCP marketplace standard terms.
- Template can say: “Termination and refunds are governed by the applicable marketplace agreement; Redwood may provide service credits at its discretion.” (Sofia can fine-tune language.)

4) Dedicated capacity
- Please ensure SKU descriptions tie to “reserved capacity units” and don’t read like an unlimited right to consume.

If Soojin updates the doc to incorporate the language notes above, RevRec is OK.

Emily Stone
Revenue Accounting
Redwood Inference


---

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 3:08 PM
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU + pricing guardrails — approvals needed (AWS/GCP refresh)

Legal notes / required edits before we lock templates:

1) Discount / pricing language
- Avoid “best price” / “guaranteed savings” wording anywhere in marketplace listing or private offer notes.
- OK to describe “cost controls” and “tools to reduce unit costs,” but no commitments.

2) Refunds
- Agree with Emily: do not promise refunds.
- We can include: “Any refunds are subject to the marketplace terms and the applicable offer; Redwood does not provide refunds except as required by law or the marketplace agreement.”

3) Credits
- Fine with Redwood-issued promotional credits, but we need a short internal policy statement that credits are discretionary, non-transferable, non-cash equivalent, and may expire.

4) Private deployment
- Make sure the marketplace SKU description does not imply we deliver on-prem software automatically. Private includes VPC and on-prem *options* subject to SOW.

If you want, I can do a quick redline pass on the aws-private-offer-template-notes.docx once the discount approval table is final.

Sofia Mendes
Commercial Counsel (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 21, 2026 at 9:22 AM
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU + pricing guardrails — approvals needed (AWS/GCP refresh)

Updated based on all feedback (thanks):

Changes made:
- Added explicit discount approval table + payment terms approval.
- Replaced “commit drawdown” phrasing with “committed spend applied to usage.”
- Added “no best price / no guaranteed savings” note for listing copy + offer templates.
- Dedicated language updated to “reserved capacity units” and removed “unlimited” phrasing.
- Private updated to “VPC/on-prem options subject to SOW.”
- Added credits policy stub (internal only) and kept “no marketplace credits” as default.

Remaining question for Jordan/Laura:
- Hosted commit minimum at $120k/yr: do we want an exception path for <$120k/yr if it’s purely to satisfy procurement (e.g., customer already at $80k run-rate, needs marketplace for renewal)?

If OK, I’ll push the final guardrails to Partnerships + update the internal enablement page.

Soojin


---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 21, 2026 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU + pricing guardrails — approvals needed (AWS/GCP refresh)

Approved with one constraint:

- Minimums stand as written.
- Exception path for Hosted commit <$120k/yr is allowed ONLY for (a) renewal via marketplace mandate or (b) strategic logo where we expect expansion within 2 quarters.
- Approvals for that exception: CRO + Finance (Laura) + documented rationale in HubSpot.

Soojin — please circulate the final guardrails as the single source of truth and make sure Partnerships uses the same language in AWS/GCP templates.

Sofia — please do the redline pass on the private offer notes and send back by Friday.

Laura/Emily — thanks. If you see any deviations in early offers, flag me immediately; I don’t want “marketplace” becoming an excuse for margin leakage.

Jordan
